entries.topic: From RAGE to Schedule Policy/Career: Schedule F (EO 13957), its revocation, EO 14171, the 2026 OPM rule, EO 14410 and the litigation

claims.text: EO 13957 (October 2020, published 26 October 2020) created Schedule F for career positions of a 'confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character' 'not normally subject to change as a result of a Presidential transition'; Biden revoked it in 2021 (EO 14003); OPM's 9 April 2024 rule guaranteed reclassified employees MSPB appeal rights

EO 14171 (20 January 2025), 'Restoring Accountability to Policy-Influencing Positions Within the Federal Workforce', reinstated EO 13957 with amendments, renamed the schedule Schedule Policy/Career and rescinded EO 14003

OPM final rule FR doc. 2026-02375 published 6 February 2026: policy-influencing positions excluded from chapter 43 performance-removal protections; 2024 appeal-rights rule rescinded; President, not OPM, moves positions; competitive appointment standards, trial periods and competitive status after two years kept

NTEU sued in 2020 and dismissed after revocation; NTEU sued again on 20 January 2025 in D.D.C.; on 17 March 2026 the court accepted NTEU's plan to amend within 14 days of an order placing positions; PEER and four unions sued in D. Md.; CRS lists the Saving the Civil Service Act (H.R. 492/S. 134) among options for Congress

EO 14410, 3 June 2026: positions listed in an appendix move to Schedule Policy/Career; they are 'exempted from the adverse action procedures'; agencies may separate for unacceptable performance or misconduct with written notice; positions 'will be filled based on merit and not political affiliation'; purpose: the President 'relies on subordinates in the executive branch to help him faithfully execute the laws'

NPR 3 June 2026: about 8,000 workers, nearly all GS-15, become at-will; OPM had estimated up to 50,000; about 4,000 political appointees for comparison; Kupor: 'This is very much about accountability' and 'a restoration, in our mind, of the democratic process'; no loyalty tests, whistleblower protections remain; Moynihan: 'It creates bubbles around policymakers'

FedSmith: 97% GS-15 or Senior Level; 229-page appendix across more than 248 units; Kupor said people could be 'removed effectively at will'; AFGE's Kelley called it 'one of the largest acts of political corruption in American history' if it stands
PEER v. Trump (D. Md., Xinis J.), joined by AFGE: second amended complaint 4 March 2026 covering EO, rule and reclassification; no preliminary injunction reported; case pending

James Sherk, a former special assistant to President Trump, defended Schedule F in June 2023: 'Every federal employee should serve at the pleasure of the president'; former officials identified 50,000 workers they would target

entries.topic: The walls between federal datasets (Privacy Act, section 6103) and their breaching in 2025-26: IRS-ICE, SSA, CMS-ICE, ORR, voter-roll suits, state limits

claims.text: DOJ: in 1974 Congress was concerned with 'curbing the illegal surveillance and investigation of individuals by federal agencies' exposed during Watergate and with 'the government's increasing use of computers' for personal data; the Act restricts disclosure of personally identifiable records

Gibbs (former IRS commissioner) helped draft the 1976 revisions of section 6103 after Nixon 'attempted to cause the IRS to provide him with confidential taxpayer information' (Article II(1) of the 1974 impeachment articles); returns became confidential unless expressly authorised

Bessent and Noem signed the IRS-ICE agreement (Monday 7 April 2025): ICE submits names and addresses for cross-checking; Treasury cited 'longstanding authorities granted by Congress'; Lyons said 'strictly for the major criminal cases'; acting IRS commissioner Melanie Krause stepping down over it, per two people familiar

About 6,300 immigrants were moved into SSA's Death Master File (renamed 'Ineligible Master File'), per an anonymous official, identified by DHS as paroled people on a watch list or with FBI records; White House: removing the 'monetary incentive' will 'encourage them to self-deport'; AP: they are in the country legally

CMS began sharing Medicaid data with ICE in June 2025; a July 2025 agreement gave DHS access to names, addresses, birth dates, ethnicities and SSNs; ICE had a policy since 2013 of not using Medicaid data for enforcement; 20 states sued; Chhabria's PI (August 2025): 'The record in this case strongly suggests that no such process occurred'

Chhabria, 29 December 2025: sharing basic biographical and contact data on people not lawfully present is 'clearly authorized by law'; allowed fields: citizenship/immigration status, address, phone, date of birth, Medicaid ID; sensitive medical information not cleared

ORR sponsor data: 2018 MOA (Trump I); barred by the Biden Foundational Rule effective 30 April 2024; bar rescinded by IFR 25 March 2025; Angelica S. v. HHS partial PI 9 June 2025 against new documentation rules, IFR itself not enjoined

DOJ sued 30 states and DC for unredacted voter rolls (UW tracker); by 13 July 2026 it had lost all 13 trial-level merits decisions and one at the Sixth Circuit; Judge Johnston: 'one is left to wonder what the real purpose was'; Ninth Circuit argued California/Oregon appeals in May 2026

DOJ argued the NVRA, HAVA and the Civil Rights Act of 1960 require states to hand over full lists including SSNs and driver's licence data for roll maintenance; Ninth Circuit 'sharply questioned' DOJ on 19 May 2026

UWCHR: Washington's law bars state agencies from sharing data for civil immigration enforcement, yet as of 13 October 2026 researchers confirmed 356 cases where Licensing data was accessed by federal agents before immigration arrests; routes include Nlets, brokers and local agencies; closing one pathway pushes agencies to another

entries.topic: NSPM-7, the Antifa order, the Bondi memo, designations, prosecutions and the nonprofit scrutiny; Detachment 201

claims.text: NSPM-7, 25 September 2025: cites the assassination of Charlie Kirk, the 2024 killing of a healthcare executive, the 2022 attempt on Justice Kavanaugh and attacks on ICE officers; Sec. 1 common threads include 'anti-Americanism, anti-capitalism, and anti-Christianity', 'support for the overthrow of the United States Government', 'extremism on migration, race, and gender'

NSPM-7 Sec. 2: JTTFs investigate 'institutional and individual funders, and officers and employees of organizations'; Treasury to 'identify and disrupt financial networks' and guide SAR filing; IRS to ensure no tax-exempt entity is 'directly or indirectly financing political violence or domestic terrorism'; Sec. 3: AG may recommend 'domestic terrorist organization' designation using 18 U.S.C. 2331(5); no First Amendment reference; 'consistent with applicable law'

Antifa order, 22 September 2025: 'I hereby designate Antifa as a domestic terrorist organization'; calls it 'a militarist, anarchist enterprise'; agencies to 'investigate, disrupt, and dismantle' and act against funders; cites no specific statute

Bondi memo, 4 December 2025, to all federal prosecutors: FBI/JTTFs to 'compile a list of groups or entities engaged in acts that may constitute domestic terrorism', reports every 30 days; cash reward system; cooperators; five-year look-back; 14-day review of Antifa holdings; tax crimes; indicators include 'opposition to law and immigration enforcement', 'radical gender ideology', 'anti-Christianity'; footnote: 'No investigation may be opened based solely on activities protected by the First Amendment'
DLA Piper: NSPM-7 creates no new legal authority; the domestic designation is not a formal legal designation; material-support, entry-bar and asset-freeze consequences attach to foreign designations

State designated Antifa Ost (Germany), FAI/FRI (Italy), Armed Proletarian Justice and Revolutionary Class Self-Defense (Greece) as SDGTs on 13 November 2025, with FTO designation effective 20 November 2025

Prairieland, Alvarado TX, 4 July 2025: police officer shot and survived; Fort Worth jury convicted 8 of 9 of material support to terrorists (predicates: destruction of government property, attempted murder of a federal officer) plus riot; prosecutors did not need to prove antifa existed; defence disputed antifa is an organization; prosecutor: on trial for conduct, not beliefs

Wyden-Warnock letter 2 September 2026: cites NY Post (27 Aug 2026) that Treasury is reviewing tax-exempt status of OSF, SPLC and CAIR under a 'blueprint', and CBS that IRS-CI is working with the FBI to scrutinize nonprofits; asks whether any organization has been recommended for examination or revocation; reports no completed revocation

Amicus brief 25 August 2026 for FIRE, Society for the Rule of Law and Cato argues DHS used NSPM-7 to infiltrate meetings, monitor encrypted chats and seize years of financial records from unions and nonprofits; says NSPM-7 'treats left-leaning political viewpoints as indicia of domestic terrorism'

Detachment 201: Shyam Sankar (Palantir CTO), Andrew Bosworth (Meta CTO), Kevin Weil (OpenAI CPO) and Bob McGrew (Thinking Machines adviser, ex-OpenAI) sworn in as Army Reserve lieutenant colonels on 13 June 2025, part-time senior advisers
Army spokesman Steve Warren (June 2025): 'It's not in our interest to show any favoritism to a company'; 'They're not making acquisition decisions'; conflict rules same as other reservists

10 June 2026: Dane Knecht (Cloudflare), Sam Pullara (Sutter Hill) and Serkan Piantino commissioned; Army: recusal 'mandatory' under Joint Ethics Regulation, OGE 450 filings, annual training, legal review per task, 'clear functional separation of duties', barred from vendor selection; first cohort advised on munitions supply chains, counter-drone and autonomy

entries.topic: Technical detail for the silo architecture diagrams: SAVE query keys and SSA link; Privacy Act computer-matching agreements

claims.text: SAVE matches people by full Social Security number or its last four digits; from May 2025 agencies could open cases with SSNs, enabling batch uploads of voter rolls and driver's-licence data; the October 2025 PIA describes integration with SSA databases including citizenship fields and the Death Master File

Under 5 U.S.C. 552a(o), records in a system of records may be disclosed for a computer matching program only under a written agreement between source and recipient agencies; SSA's agreements are approved by its Data Integrity Board and announced in the Federal Register
